# Protected source preparation — disabled

The live public-feature publisher remains unchanged. This preparation does not make dependencies, documentation, accounts, payments or backend changes automatically deployable.

`pages-protected-scope.mjs` classifies exact Git trees without loading source dependencies. Development updates may change only devDependencies and npm lock v3 development nodes. Both production resolution graphs (including optional/peer edges), runtime bytes, scripts, engines, overrides, registries, workspaces and root metadata stay fixed. Changed installation hooks are rejected. Registry integrity identifies bytes, not package safety. Clean preparation uses `npm ci --ignore-scripts`; review any required hook separately.

The reader-document route permits only exact old-to-canonical URL-prefix substitutions in six named Markdown files. It preserves suffixes/prose and the README deployment section, rejects missing route equivalents, and grants no provider-deployment authority. The auth-provider setup document is excluded. Documentation-aware main routing must be reviewed before those changes merge; the live public guard currently rejects them.

The executable artifact preparation recomputes scope after tests, binds the accepted baseline artifact/source, independently validates both workers, requires all other runtime files to remain byte-identical, and consumes exact-tree first-attempt contained browser/app reports. A changed runtime output is a separate review boundary, not a hash to repin. A PR test-merge SHA is retained distinctly from its head even when the trees match.

## Credential and activation boundary

The staged workflow is outside workflow discovery and has an unusable placeholder controller SHA. It is not enabled. It contains no provider credential or deployment job. Existing app defaults, publishing credentials, public path guards and repository settings are untouched.

Before a reusable dependency publisher can activate, independently review the trusted bootstrap/controller and main-route discriminator; bind an actual exact-tree review record under the applicable authorization; perform secret-free build/tests; validate immutable candidate bytes; revalidate review using dependency-free trusted code in a separate token-bearing step; then reuse existing preview byte/header/case acceptance and exact-artifact promotion, current-production checks, shared serialization and uncertain-outcome handling. No prepared JSON flag substitutes for any of these gates. The new route cannot authorize its own bootstrap. A new consequential acceptance record is distinct from PR #37's specific approval.

Rollback must use a preserved previously reviewed artifact with a fresh current-production check and explicit authorization. Never blindly roll back a collision or uncertain provider write. No automatic rollback is activated here.

## Other protected categories

Authentication/account releases need an independently approved supported runtime design, migration and session/authorization acceptance. The previously denied stale-session/callback/consumer implementation remains stopped and is not an input to this route.

Billing needs approved real payment semantics and sandbox/provider acceptance before any live activation; transactions and financial/access changes retain action-time approval. Backend/private releases require exact schema/RLS/identity mappings, disposable migration/restore proof and an approved hosted operation; source CI does not authorize database writes. Release controls need independent bootstrap review and applicable security approval. Minors, retention/deletion, notifications, credentials and production access remain gated separately.

These are explicit rejection boundaries, not enabled generic release lanes or claims of completed provider acceptance. No new environment, credentials or broader token scope is needed for the local preparation proven here.
